Plot gallery

Source: vignettes/plotting.Rmd
plotting.Rmd
library(lifr)
library(ggplot2)
demo <- system.file("extdata", "demo", package = "lifr")
lif <- lif_import(demo, verbose = FALSE)
lif <- lif_zero_shallow(lif, depth = 1)

Every plotting function returns a ggplot (or a patchwork of them), so you can add layers, change labels, or save with ggsave() as usual. All of them share theme_lifr().

Depth profiles

One boring: lif_plot()

Depth runs down the page. When the log carries an emission colour, the trace is filled with it and a colour strip sits left of zero; otherwise a single fill is used.

lif_plot(lif, "LIF-11")

Fix the signal axis to compare borings on the same scale, or cap the depth:

lif_plot(lif, "LIF-05", ymax = 100, xmax = 25)

Every boring: lif_plot_all() 

lif_plot_all(lif, ncol = 4)

layout = "list" returns one full lif_plot() per boring instead, and output_file writes the facet figure straight to a PNG.

Multi-channel: lif_overview()

LIF beside conductivity and pressure on a shared depth axis. Channels the boring did not record are skipped.

lif_overview(lif, "LIF-06")

Input versus edited: qc_compare() 

edited <- lif_keep(lif, "LIF-10", top = 8, bottom = 24)
qc_compare(lif, edited)[["LIF-10"]]

Plan-view maps

boring_map()

Each boring is a marker sized by the square root of its peak signal, so the site’s pattern reads even in greyscale, and labelled with its name and peak. Non-detects are hollow circles. A north arrow and scale bar sit in whichever corners overlap the fewest borings.

boring_map(lif, site_name = "Demo site", figure_date = "2026-09-04",
           preparer = "Field team")

use_instrument_color = TRUE fills each marker with the emission colour at the depth of peak signal, the product signature analysts read directly:

boring_map(lif, use_instrument_color = TRUE)

Restrict the peak to a depth window:

boring_map(lif, depth_min = 12, depth_max = 20, use_instrument_color = TRUE)

Other useful arguments: nd_threshold (peaks at or below it are non-detects), size_by_signal = FALSE for uniform markers, coord_units for metric sites, crs_label for the caption, repel = FALSE to skip ggrepel, and output_file to save.

Aerial imagery under the map

With a projected CRS and network access, fetch_basemap() pulls a public-domain USGS National Map tile for the site (US coverage only) and boring_map() draws it under the markers; labels switch to white with a dark halo.

bm <- fetch_basemap(lif, crs = 3452)   # NAD83 / Louisiana South (ftUS)
boring_map(lif, basemap = bm)

fetch_basemap() needs the sf and png packages and returns NULL with a warning when it cannot fetch, so a map call with basemap = NULL simply draws without imagery.

depth_slice_map()

Colour each boring by the aggregate (default maximum) of a channel inside a depth band. Borings with no readings in the band are grey crosses, so “not sampled here” is never mistaken for “no boring here”.

depth_slice_map(lif, depth_range = c(12, 20))

depth_slice_map(lif, depth_range = c(5, 10), channel = "ec", agg_fn = median)

Site charts

These are the figures the site report embeds; each is also available on its own.

chart_max_response(lif, thresholds = c(1, 10, 50))

chart_peak_by_boring(lif)

chart_hp_histogram(lif)

chart_ec_histogram(lif)

export_site_charts() writes whichever of them the data supports as PNGs in one call.

Customising

Everything is a ggplot. Add layers or override labels:

lif_plot(lif, "LIF-11") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 10, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  labs(title = "LIF-11 with a 10 %RE screening line",
       subtitle = "Demo site, September 2026")

Use the package theme on your own figures:

re <- re_feet(lif)
ggplot(re, aes(x = reorder(boring, re_feet), y = re_feet)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#6E7F4E") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "RE-feet (integrated signal)",
       title = "Integrated LIF response by boring") +
  theme_lifr()

Save any plot with ggplot2::ggsave():

ggsave("boring_map.png", boring_map(lif), width = 8, height = 7, dpi = 200)
